articles.title: An election of firsts: America's melting pot cooks MAGA
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: From the first Black woman governor and the first Muslim senator to a Native American woman taking the governor's
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: From the first Black woman governor and the first Muslim senator to a Native American woman taking the governor's mansion and an openly gay man entering the Senate, the 2026 midterms have produced a remarkable roll call of political trailblazers.At first glance, Donald Trump's midterm humiliation was hardly unexpected. American presidents have a habit of getting walloped halfway through their terms. Barack Obama suffered a particularly brutal drubbing in 2010, losing 63 House seats. In comparison, Trump's Republican Party has given up only around 30 seats.But the significance of this election goes well beyond the familiar American tradition of voters giving the president's party a midterm spanking. Look more closely, and something rather extraordinary emerges. This was an election that challenged the political, cultural and demographic assumptions of Trumpism. In a country increasingly defined by its diversity -- racial, religious, ethnic and cultural -- voters sent an unmistakable message about who gets to occupy the corridors of power, rejecting the MAGA movement’s unsubtle effort to enforce white male primacy.There were Black, Latino, Native American, Muslim and openly gay winners. Women broke barriers in states that had never elected a woman governor. A Muslim doctor made history in the Senate. A Native American woman moved from the lieutenant governor's mansion to the Senate. And a Black woman who once presided over Atlanta is about to preside over Georgia.In short, America did not merely elect a new crop of politicians. It considerably expanded the guest list at a political establishment that has historically been rather selective about whom it lets in. Here is an extensive roll call of the historic firsts from the Nov midterms, covering the Senate, House, and gubernatorial races.Senate: Breaking the ultimate political glass ceiling1. First Muslim elected to the US Senate — Abdul El-Sayed (Michigan): The physician, epidemiologist and former Wayne County health director defeated Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim ever elected to the US Senate. His victory was particularly significant after a campaign marked by attacks on his Muslim identity.2. First openly gay man elected to the US Senate — Chris Pappas (New Hampshire): The Democratic congressman becomes the first openly gay man elected to the upper chamber. He will join the Senate alongside his husband, Vann Bentley, after defeating Republican John Sununu.3. First Native American woman elected to the US Senate — Peggy Flanagan (Minnesota): A member of the White Earth Nation and Minnesota's outgoing lieutenant governor, Flanagan becomes the first Native American woman to serve in the Senate.4. Three Black women serving simultaneously in the Senate for the first time: Juliana Stratton's victory in Illinois means that, beginning in January 2027, three Black women will serve together in the Senate: Stratton, Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland and Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware.5. First woman elected to the US Senate from South Carolina -- Annie Andrews: The Democratic pediatrician becomes the first woman elected to represent South Carolina in the Senate. She also becomes the state's first Democratic woman senator.6. First Republican woman elected to the Senate from Louisiana — Julia Letlow: Her victory makes her the first Republican woman to represent Louisiana in the Senate, and the first woman to hold the state's Senate seat since 2015.7. First Black senator from Mississippi since Reconstruction — Scott Colom (Mississippi): This is potentially one of the most consequential historical breakthroughs. Colom's victory would make him the first Black senator elected from Mississippi since Blanche K. Bruce, who served during Reconstruction in the 1870s.Governors: The biggest breakthrough of allPerhaps nowhere was the transformation more visible than in gubernatorial races. Several states elected someone from a demographic group that had never before occupied their highest elected office.1. First Black woman elected governor in American history — Keisha Lance Bottoms (Georgia): The former Atlanta mayor has made history twice over: she is the first Black woman elected governor anywhere in the US, and the first Black person and first woman elected governor of Georgia. She defeated Republican billionaire Rick Jackson.2. First Black governor of Florida — Byron Donalds (Florida): The Republican congressman becomes Florida's first Black governor. His victory also gives Republicans a milestone of their own in an election otherwise dominated by Democratic breakthroughs.3. First Native American woman elected governor — Deb Haaland (New Mexico): The former Interior Secretary and member of the Laguna Pueblo becomes the first Native American woman to govern a US state. She was also one of the first two Native American women elected to Congress in 2018.4. First Latina governor of Texas — Gina Hinojosa (Texas): The Democrat defeated Greg Abbott, ending a 31-year Republican hold on the Texas governorship. Her victory is particularly striking in a state whose political establishment has long been dominated by Republicans, despite its large Hispanic population.5. First elected Latino governor of California — Xavier Becerra (California): The former US Health and Human Services secretary, the son of Mexican immigrants, becomes the first Latino elected governor of California. (Romualdo Pacheco, California's first Latino governor, assumed office in 1875 through succession rather than being elected governor)6. First Black governor of Wisconsin — David Crowley (Wisconsin): The Milwaukee County executive becomes the first Black person elected governor of Wisconsin. His victory is another significant breakthrough in a state that has been a pivotal battleground in national politics.7. First Black governor of Nevada — Aaron Ford (Nevada): The state's attorney general becomes its first Black governor. He also becomes the first Black governor of any state west of the Mississippi River.8. First woman elected governor of Ohio — Amy Acton (Ohio): The former Ohio health director becomes the first woman elected governor of Ohio and the first Jewish governor in the state's history after defeating Vivek Ramaswamy. Nancy Hollister briefly served as governor through succession in 1998–99, so Acton is not technically the first woman ever to hold the office.9. First woman elected governor of Minnesota — Amy Klobuchar (Minnesota): The veteran senator becomes the first woman elected to Minnesota's governorship, another state that had never elected a woman to its top office.10. First woman elected governor of Tennessee — Marsha Blackburn (Tennessee): The Republican senator makes history in a state that has never elected a woman governor. Her victory is a reminder that the election's gender breakthroughs were not exclusively Democratic.11. Five Black governors serving simultaneously for the first time in American history: his is a particularly striking collective milestone. The five are:Keisha Lance Bottoms — Georgia.Byron Donalds — Florida.David Crowley — Wisconsin.Aaron Ford — Nevada.Wes Moore — Maryland, who was already in office.For a country that has had relatively few Black governors in its entire history, having five serving concurrently is a remarkable change. It also makes the milestone bipartisan, with Donalds representing the Republicans and the other four Democrats.12. First governor-elect to have publicly spoken about surviving childhood sexual abuse — Amy Acton (Ohio).This deserves a separate mention, although it is not a conventional racial or gender first. Acton has spoken publicly about her traumatic childhood, including sexual abuse by her stepfather between the ages of approximately 9 and 12, neglect and periods of homelessness. Her personal history became an extraordinary issue in the campaign after Vivek Ramaswamy's camp aired an attack advertisement featuring her estranged mother disputing her account. Acton publicly defended her account, and the controversy generated considerable sympathy and attention.Other noteworthy milestones beyond individual firsts1. At least 102 women from the Democratic Party alone have officially won House races, shattering the previous party record of 95 seats and marking the first time in American history that more than 100 women from a single party will serve in the House simultaneously. With many results still due, and adding 20 republican women who have won, America is on track to beat the record for female representation in the House (127/435 seats) which was set in 2024.2. First time two of America's largest states will have Latino governors simultaneously: California's Xavier Becerra and Texas's Gina Hinojosa will take office in two states with enormous Latino populations. The symbolism is quite remarkable: the two states that were once part of Mexico will be governed by politicians of Mexican-American heritage.3. Four states elect their first women governors in the same election: Georgia, Minnesota, Ohio and Tennessee all elected women to their highest executive office for the first time: Keisha Lance Bottoms, Amy Klobuchar, Amy Acton and Marsha Blackburn respectively.4. Record number of women governors: The election produced an unprecedented expansion of women in gubernatorial offices. There will now be 17 women governors in the United States; almost a third of America's 50 states will be governed by women.5. New Mexico elected an all-women-of-color gubernatorial ticket: Deb Haaland and Lieutenant Governor-elect Stephanie Garcia Richard become the first all-women-of-color ticket elected to govern a state.You use AI every day. articles.title: Swinney criticises UK move to ban new North Sea drilling
articles.summary: The first minister has told Holyrood fossil fuels will be required "for some years to come".
articles.body:
First Minister John Swinney says he does not support the UK government's plans to ban any new exploration for oil and gas in the North Sea.

The SNP leader told MSPs fossil fuels would be required "for some years to come".

He argued there was a "rational" case for further exploration if the project's carbon emissions was lower than using imported fuel.

The Scottish government, in its 2023 energy strategy , set out a presumption against new oil and gas drilling.

If passed by MPs, the UK government's Energy Independence Bill would remove the North Sea Transition Authority's ability to grant fresh oil and gas licences, in line with a Labour manifesto pledge not to grant permission for new fields.

It does not affect the decision on whether to allow drilling at Rosebank off Shetland - the UK's largest known untapped field - which was approved in 2022 before being subject to legal challenges.

Swinney has repeatedly refused to be drawn on whether he explicitly supports drilling at Rosebank.

UK government to outlaw new North Sea drilling

Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

Asked about the bill at First Minister's Questions, Swinney said: "The government has set out our view that because we are going to be using oil and gas for years to come there is a rational basis for considering oil and gas developments within our own jurisdiction if they offer lower carbon emissions than imported oil and gas."

He told parliament the UK government's bill includes several measures his government supports, adding: "But we do not support the provisions of that bill in relation to the position on the granting of new licences."

Swinney said this was because "any particular applications need to be considered in relation to their impact on our carbon reduction target and given the fact we are going to be using oil and gas for some years to come".

Decisions on new oil and gas licences are made by the UK government.

However, under Nicola Sturgeon's leadership, the Scottish government proposed a presumption against new oil and gas developments.

The Swinney administration appears to have shifted away from that position, especially since the outbreak of war in the Middle East.

Scottish ministers nevertheless continue to stress any oil and gas developments should be compatible with the government's ambitions to cut carbon emissions over time.

Scottish Greens co-leader Gillian Mackay described Swinney's comments as a "shocking U-turn".

She said: "It is a huge departure from only a few years ago when the Scottish government was committed to a presumption against oil and gas.

"When even the UK government is taking a stronger position, it shows how far the SNP has drifted. It is a shameful retreat and a slap in the face for future generations."

Although the UK bill would prevent the granting of new licences, it would allow existing oil and gas fields to provide additional production from within its existing boundaries, or in nearby areas.

The UK government said the move could produce about 60 million barrels of oil and support hundreds of jobs.

It vowed to sustain "growth and investment across North Sea communities as the energy sector transitions".

The wide-ranging bill would also formally scrap gas standing charges and introduce reforms designed to speed up grid connections.

Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said the bill would help to "build a clean energy future which people feel in their pockets, households and communities, ensuring support reaches those who need it most".

The SNP will seek to remove the ban on new oil and gas drilling from the bill. If this does not happen they will oppose the legislation despite supporting other measures contained within it.

articles.title: A Washington couple signed a prenup when the husband was worth over $15 million and his wife had $175,000; after disputes over a Porsche and divorce legal fees, an appeals court broadened the scope for attorney fee awards
articles.summary: Washington’s Court of Appeals has given trial courts more room to order a wealthier spouse to pay a poorer spouse’s legal fees, even when a prenuptial
articles.body: Washington’s Court of Appeals has given trial courts more room to order a wealthier spouse to pay a poorer spouse’s legal fees, even when a prenuptial agreement says each side must cover its own costs. The ruling, filed on 29 October by Division Three of the Washington Court of Appeals, clarifies that judges are not limited to awarding fees for work directly related to parenting or child support. They may also award reasonable fees incurred in other aspects of the divorce, despite a prenuptial agreement containing a fee-waiver clause. The court reached this conclusion while reviewing the case of a couple whose prenup required each spouse to bear their own legal costs in the event of a divorce.A prenup with a fee waiverIn 2018, the Washington couple signed an antenuptial agreement. At the time, the husband’s net worth exceeded $15 million, while the wife’s was about $175,000. In the prenup, they agreed to pay their own attorney fees in any dissolution or maintenance case. They married in July 2019 and had a child. The wife was a stay-at-home mother for most of the marriage. According to the filed opinion, she drained her savings paying half of the family’s monthly expenses during the marriage.Separation and divorceA couple of years into the marriage, they hit rock bottom. The wife left in July 2022 and obtained a domestic violence protection order. The husband soon filed for legal separation and then filed for dissolution.One unusual aspect of the case involves a 2018 Porsche 911 Cabriolet. The husband bought the car and gifted it to the wife during their marriage. He also posted it on social media. The court ordered him to return the wife’s personal items, including the car, within 30 days. He did neither. He told the court that the car was at a dealership, but it was actually with an exotic car consignment dealer, where it had been for six months before the order. The court found Mark in contempt four times over the course of the case and found him intransigent three times. It imposed $5,000 in sanctions after the Porsche episode.The wife asked for attorney feesIn April 2023, the wife sought her first award of legal fees, having already incurred $131,229.05 in fees and costs. The court ordered the husband to pay $35,000. In January 2024, she sought a second award of $189,253.24, arguing that the agreement could not prevent her from recovering fees related to parenting issues. The court ordered $40,000 for child-related litigation.The wife later asked the court to reconsider and filed a supplemental declaration stating that she owed her attorney $277,710.29. Her lawyer wrote that his firm had borrowed heavily to cover the shortfall. The court eventually awarded $188,911.49, reducing the request by offsetting expert and guardian ad litem fees, applying the husband’s sanctions and cutting charges it considered wasteful or duplicative.The question was really about how broadly the court’s 1999 decision in In re Marriage of Burke should be applied. In that case, the court ruled that a prenuptial agreement cannot prevent a parent from seeking legal fees for disputes involving parenting plans.The husband in this case argued that the ruling applied only to those matters. However, the court disagreed. It said judges should have the discretion to award legal fees in divorce cases involving parenting plans and child support, even when the fees relate to other aspects of the divorce. The majority explained that without this discretion, a wealthier spouse could prolong other disputes until the financially weaker spouse could no longer afford a lawyer.The appeals court did not decide whether the specific legal fee award to the wife was correct. It sent the case back to the trial court for further consideration. On appeal, the court said the wife may recover reasonable fees, although the amount is a factual matter for the trial judge.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Agnipath: A new version
articles.summary: Giving soldiers more time to serve is a good idea. But the Army must still find ways to become more modern and efficient.
articles.body: Giving soldiers more time to serve is a good idea. But the Army must still find ways to become more modern and efficient.The government has changed its Agnipath scheme, which was introduced four years ago to recruit young soldiers into the armed forces. Under the new plan, Agniveers will have a better chance of joining the Army permanently, depending on whether they want to continue and meet the selection requirements.The original Agnipath scheme was designed to make the armed forces younger and more modern. It also aimed to reduce the number of soldiers and save money on salaries and pensions. This would leave more money to buy modern weapons and equipment.Since the One-Rank-One-Pension scheme began in 2014-15, the money spent on military salaries and pensions has increased greatly. It now takes up more than half of India's yearly defence budget. This is a big concern because the armed forces also need money to modernise.China has made similar changes to its military. It reduced the size of its army from 23L soldiers to 20L. Its aim was to build a smaller, faster and more technologically advanced force.India also wanted to make its armed forces more modern. But the original Agnipath scheme faced several problems.First, in states such as UP, Uttarakhand, Himachal and Punjab, joining the Army is often a family tradition. For many young people, it is also a chance to get a secure job and improve their family's life. Under the original scheme, 75% of Agniveers had to leave after four years. GOI had hoped they would find other jobs, but enough suitable jobs were not available.Second, some military experts felt that four years was too short to train soldiers properly. They were also worried that Agniveers and permanent soldiers working together might feel unfairly treated because their salaries and benefits were very different.There was another concern: trained Agniveers leaving the Army might be recruited by anti-social groups or even become mercenaries (people paid to fight for others).GOI’s latest decision tries to solve some of these problems. The 75% of Agniveers who are not selected for permanent service will now be offered two more years in the armed forces. They may also get another chance to join permanently later.However, one big problem remains: the growing cost of soldiers' salaries and pensions. If the government simply returns to the old system of keeping more soldiers permanently, it may become difficult to find enough money for modern weapons and equipment.One possible solution is to slowly reduce the number of soldiers recruited every year over the next five years, instead of making a big change all at once.Of course, if India had enough good-paying jobs for young people leaving the Army, this problem would be much easier to solve. But creating enough jobs remains one of the country's biggest challenges.India needs strong armed forces because it faces security challenges along two borders. GOI must find the right balance between having enough soldiers, spending wisely and building a modern military.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

articles.title: Accused held in Araria rape case
articles.summary: Man arrested in Bihar’s Araria for alleged rape of 20-year-old; complaint filed Nov 4 amid claims of panchayat pressure to settle for Rs 1 lakh.
articles.body: Patna: A man was arrested in Araria district on Wednesday night for allegedly raping a 20-year-old woman after entering her house. The incident occurred on Nov 1 when the woman was alone at home. The accused allegedly gagged her before sexually assaulting her and fleeing the spot, police said on Thursday.Police arrested the accused, identified as Dinesh Biswas, after the survivor lodged a complaint on Nov 4. The case has sparked allegations that attempts were made to suppress the matter through a village panchayat.According to the complaint, the woman was cleaning her house around 2 pm while her mother was away for daily-wage work. The family also runs a grocery shop outside their residence. Biswas, a resident of the same village, allegedly arrived in a vehicle, parked it outside the shop and entered the house.The complaint alleges that he stuffed a piece of cloth into the woman’s mouth to prevent her from raising an alarm before sexually assaulting her. He then fled the spot. After her mother returned, the survivor informed her about the incident. The family subsequently sought action against the accused.However, the survivor’s sister alleged that local residents convened a panchayat instead of immediately approaching the police. She claimed that former and current panchayat representatives, along with some villagers, held meetings over three days in an attempt to settle the matter.The family alleged that pressure was exerted on them to accept a settlement of Rs 1 lakh and not pursue the case. No agreement was reached. articles.body: Bengaluru: The high court Thursday ordered the issuance of notices to the state govt and Congress’ Anekal MLA B Shivanna in response to a public interest litigation (PIL) challenging the latter’s nomination as chairperson of Karnataka State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB).A division bench comprising Justices Anu Sivaraman and KS Bharath Kumar directed the respondents to file their response to the petition filed by Sudha Katwa, a Bengaluru-based advocate.According to the petitioner, KSPCB rules prescribe a selection committee process, open advertisement in at least three national newspapers and recommendation of three suitable candidates. articles.title: Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami approves 3% DA hike for state employees, raises rate to 63%
articles.summary: DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Thursday approved a 3% hike in Dearness Allowance (DA) for state government employees,
articles.body: DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Thursday approved a 3% hike in Dearness Allowance (DA) for state government employees, increasing the rate from 60% to 63% with effect from July 1, 2026.According to the chief minister's office, the Government of India had earlier raised the DA rate by 3% points to 63%, effective July 1, 2026, for employees drawing salaries under the 7th Central Pay Commission.Following the Centre's decision, Dhami approved the proposal to extend the same DA rate to state government employees.The decision will also benefit eligible employees working in local bodies, aided educational institutions, state universities and technical educational institutions, as well as those drawing salaries under UGC pay scales.Following the chief minister's approval, the difference in DA for the period between July 1, 2026, and October 31, 2026, will be paid to eligible employees in cash as arrears.The approval follows the Centre's announcement of a 3% DA hike for its employees, taking the rate from 60% to 63% with effect from July 1, 2026.The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the additional DA instalment for Central Government employees and Dearness Relief (DR) for pensioners on October 28, providing relief amid rising prices.The revision is expected to benefit around 48.54 lakh Central Government employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners across the country.According to the Central Government, the combined annual financial implication of the DA and DR hike will be Rs 10,016.10 crore, adding to government expenditure.The additional DA and DR instalment was approved in line with the accepted formula based on the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission.Dearness Allowance is paid to serving government employees to help offset the impact of inflation on their cost of living. Dearness Relief serves a similar purpose for pensioners, helping them manage the impact of rising prices on their pension income.With the latest revision, eligible Central Government employees and pensioners will receive an additional three percentage points over the earlier rate of 60% of their basic pay or pension, respectively.(With inputs from ANI)Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. articles.title: War of Words Between Suvendu Adhikari and Abhishek Banerjee After Rs 1.02 Crore Cash Seizure in Diamond Harbour
articles.summary: Cash worth Rs 1.02 crore seized from Sarisha office sparks BJP-TMC spat; Abhishek Banerjee alleges police planted evidence, CM Adhikari attacks TMC.
articles.body: Kolkata: A war of words ensued between CM Suvendu Adhikari and TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee over the wads of cash found and seized by cops at Sarisha in Diamond Harbour on Wednesday. While the CM described the haul as “an hour’s income” for the kingpin of the illegal financial operation, Banerjee alleged police planted fabricated evidence to frame his party.CM said Trinamool had siphoned off so much money that “they don’t even remember where they stashed it.” “To them, such sums are merely a day’s or an hour’s worth of money,” he said, alleging large-scale diversion of state revenue.The Diamond Harbour ASP had displayed a haul of Rs 1,02,79,000 seized from a party office in Sarisha. Police said they had been led to the location by Banerjee’s aide Sumit Roy while he was being questioned.Abhishek alleged the cash seizure was part of a plot to manufacture evidence against him and his party. The premises were vandalised by BJP workers six months ago by BJP workers and subsequently turned into a crime scene for investigation.“The deliberate planting of fake and fabricated evidence at a property vandalised six months ago by BJP goons… is a brazen attempt to subvert justice, manipulate investigation and misuse the machinery of law,” he said.Speaking at a news conference with Shamim Ahmed — the TMC neta linked to the office where the seizure took place — Abhishek said Ahmed had been called to the Diamond Harbour SP’s office and threatened. He was asked to either sign documents implicating Banerjee or face arrest.Abhishek further alleged that Ritabrata Banerjee, who leads the rebel TMC block, also advised Shamim to give false testimony against him.“I have documentary evidence of police cars visiting the office on Nov 2. I believe they planted the money then. articles.title: 9-day stand-off ends, Daljit cremated in Mansa village
articles.summary: Daljit Singh cremated in Mansa after 9-day standoff; HC ordered second post-mortem at PGIMER. Punjab announces Rs 50 lakh relief and job for wife.
articles.body: Mansa: The mortal remains of 35-year-old Daljit Singh were cremated at his native Bhamme Kalan village in Mansa on Thursday, ending a nine-day standoff involving legal battles, two autopsies and violent clashes.The cremation took place following an order from the Punjab and Haryana high court directing a fresh post-mortem at PGIMER, Chandigarh, after the family disputed an earlier autopsy performed at AIIMS, Bathinda.His death on Oct 27, allegedly due to a drug overdose, had triggered protests and a political row over the drug menace in Punjab. Police, however, had registered a murder case and arrested three suspects. The next day, police intercepted protesters attempting to take Daljit’s body to a demonstration site seeking justice for slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa, triggering a clash. Police seized the body and conducted an initial post-mortem at AIIMS, Bathinda, with the father’s consent, exposing a split within the family as other relatives joined the ongoing anti-drug protests in Mansa.Several protesters were subsequently charged with attempt to murder, and two prominent activists, Lakha Sidhana and Mohanjit Singh Sheron, were arrested.The deadlock broke late Wednesday after the state govt reached an agreement with the Parvinder Singh Jhota Insaaf Committee. The Punjab govt announced Rs 50 lakh in financial compensation and a job at the Mansa deputy commissioner’s office for Daljit’s wife, Paramjit Kaur.Family members, including his father Jarnail Singh, mother Chhinder Kaur, wife Paramjit Kaur and sister Amarjeet Kaur, attended the final rites after bringing the body directly from PGIMER.Police said administrative procedures are underway to secure the release of Sidhana and Sheron from jail, following assurances from assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan and agriculture minister Gurmeet Singh Khudian. Their release remains a prerequisite for the post-mortem and scheduled Friday cremation of Jhota, who was killed on Oct 13.2 AUTOPSIESDaljit Singh (35) died on Oct 27; while family alleged he died of a drug overdose, police registered a murder case and arrested three suspects.Protests broke out after police seized the body; activists Lakha Sidhana and Mohanjit Singh Sheron were arrested.A second autopsy was conducted at Chandigarh’s PGIMER following Punjab and Haryana HC ordersPunjab announced Rs 50 lakh compensation and a govt job for Daljit’s wifeYou Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: No free sanitary napkin again in Delhi govt schools, alleges complaint
articles.summary: Complaint alleges Delhi government schools have again stopped free sanitary pad distribution since Sept under Kishori Yojana, despite HC and SC directives.
articles.body: New Delhi: Free sanitary napkin distribution in Delhi govt schools has allegedly stopped again, leaving girl students without supplies since Sept, states a representation sent to the education department.Under Kishori Yojana, girls studying in classes VI to XII in govt and govt-aided schools in the city are entitled to one packet containing 10 sanitary pads every month for free. Planning department documents record that the scheme was launched in Nov 2011 to support menstrual hygiene among schoolgirls.The department’s scheme description also sets out a decentralised procurement arrangement. Heads of govt schools are empowered to buy sanitary napkins through the govt e-marketplace (GeM) and distribute them. For govt-aided schools, procurement and distribution are assigned to the district deputy directors of education.Delhi High Court, on July 6, 2022, directed uninterrupted supplies while disposing of a petition by civil rights group Social Jurist. During hearings, govt said school heads and education officials had been empowered and provided funds to procure pads through GeM as an interim arrangement while a tender was being finalised.This is not the first subsequent complaint of disruption. In Dec 2025, TOI reported allegations that supplies had stopped for three months. Directorate of Education (DoE) issued an order on Dec 24 asking school heads to continue procuring and distributing sanitary napkins.The fresh allegation also comes after Supreme Court’s Jan 30, 2026, judgement directing states and Union territories to ensure free sanitary napkins in govt and privately managed schools. It required supplies to be readily accessible through vending machines or designated distribution arrangements within schools.Advocate Ashok Aggarwal, associated with Social Jurist, has written to the education secretary seeking urgent intervention over the alleged two-month disruption. “A two-month gap in supply has severely disrupted the routine hygiene of these young students, causing grave consequences,” Aggarwal wrote. He alleged that the interruption violated the high court’s directions.The representation has sought swift action to safeguard students’ health and education. His complaint does not identify the schools affected or explain the reason for the alleged stoppage. Its extent, procurement status and DoE's current response remain to be established. There was no immediate response from the education department.The representation urges the department to treat the matter as a priority, describing the alleged disruption as a severe lapse.
